title: Predicting motor recovery using surface electromyography in people with severe motor impairment after stroke: A prospective cohort study protocol✰
author: Farah, J, et al.

steps.title: Screen patients for eligibility
steps.instruction: Within the first week after stroke onset, consecutively screen all admitted acute‑stroke patients for eligibility according to the study criteria.

steps.title: Log screening outcomes
steps.instruction: Maintain a screening log documenting the number of patients screened, the number included, the number excluded (with reasons), and the number who decline participation.

steps.title: Obtain informed consent
steps.instruction: Approach patients who meet inclusion criteria, explain the study, and obtain written informed consent for participation.

steps.title: Schedule baseline measurement
steps.instruction: Arrange for the participant’s baseline measurements to be recorded on the day after consent is obtained.

steps.title: Collect raw sEMG signals
steps.instruction: Record surface electromyography (sEMG) from the paretic side at two time points: (a) within 7 days of stroke onset and (b) again at 30 days after stroke onset.

steps.title: Perform sEMG recordings in quiet room
steps.instruction: During hospitalization, conduct all sEMG recordings in a quiet room adjacent to the stroke unit; during follow‑up, perform recordings in the physiotherapy department.

steps.title: Process sEMG data
steps.instruction: Import raw sEMG data into LabChart version 8.1.30, normalize the %Maximal Voluntary Contraction (%MVC) by calculating (mean RMS / max RMS) × 100, and use this normalized value for analysis.

steps.title: Compute mean RMS per trial
steps.instruction: For each 10‑second trial during task execution, compute the mean RMS; then average the mean RMS values across all trials for the participant.

steps.title: Conduct clinical outcome assessments
steps.instruction: At 1 month and 3 months after stroke onset, assess each participant with the following instruments: Fugl‑Meyer Assessment (FMA), Action Research Arm Test (ARAT), Functional Ambulation Category (FAC), 10‑meter Walk Test (10MWT), Mini BEST, and Stroke Impact Scale (SIS) version 3.0.

steps.title: Maintain assessor blinding
steps.instruction: Ensure that assessors performing the 1‑month and 3‑month clinical outcome assessments are blinded to baseline sEMG measurements, and that the neurophysiotherapist acquiring sEMG data is blinded to all follow‑up outcomes.

steps.title: Statistical analysis plan
steps.instruction: Analyze data in R Studio: test normality with the Kolmogorov‑Smirnov test, present normally distributed data as mean ± SD and non‑normal data as median with interquartile range; use Spearman or Pearson correlations for predictor‑outcome relationships; develop the prognostic model with elastic‑net penalised regression to achieve coefficient shrinkage and reduce overfitting.
